purpose: Technical checks for the SQLite implementation experiment; not a new literature-search batch

sources.title: Transaction
sections_read: 3 Response To Errors Within A Transaction
sources.finding: Only one simultaneous writer; BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires a write transaction or fails busy. Errors require explicit rollback handling.
sources.use: Read permission only after BEGIN IMMEDIATE; update permission and effects through the same write discipline; no fairness claim.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.finding: Rollback-mode atomic commit uses journaling and synchronization and depends on storage, locking and OS behavior.
sources.use: Justifies a same-database transaction boundary conditionally; process-exit tests do not verify the database engine or power-loss durability.

sources.title: PRAGMA synchronous
sources.finding: EXTRA adds directory synchronization after deleting the rollback journal; FULL alone has filesystem-dependent rollback-mode durability.
sources.use: Each connection sets synchronous=EXTRA; actual bundled SQLite reports 3. This is configuration evidence, not a tested power-failure result.

sources.title: sqlite3 — DB-API 2.0 interface for SQLite databases
sections_read: How to use the connection context manager
sources.finding: isolation_level=None permits explicit transaction control. A connection context manager commits or rolls back but does not close the connection.
sources.use: Explicit SQL BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; test-fixture connection cleanup corrected after a Windows file-lock failure.

sources.title: http.server — HTTP servers
sources.finding: The standard-library HTTP server is intended for limited use and is not recommended for production.
sources.use: Ephemeral loopback testing only; server-side token role mapping is our implementation, not a Python-provided authorization theorem.
